title: IFX I2-D: publish the curated v4-adoption package and the exact 0.5.2 bundle to main
goal: Publish the exact reviewed 0.5.2 bundle and production review, the V4 evidence producers, the ci/ staging and aggregate scripts, the proposal and specimen, and the receipts into docs/guards/v4-adoption on main through one V3-judged pull request, and prove the published bytes are the certified ones, without installing a workflow, changing the ruleset or activating anything.
acceptanceCriteria: Every remote step is separately authorized; no force push, --admin, ruleset or bypass change; the ruleset equals the I2-C snapshot.
The publication PR's final head passes all 13 required contexts with no protected-change obligation.

docs/guards/v4-adoption on main holds exactly the RD1 set, every file equal to its development-branch source blob except the authored main README; the bundle equals the certified 0.5.2 bundle file by file (manifest a2f619a3) and the review is 38eb775a.
A local composition of the published bundle gives package 0fab0676; the specimen's input checks pass on autocrlf true and false checkouts.
No workflow installed, nothing activated; P10.GATE, cutover and V3 retirement stay false.
risks: A published file could differ from the certified bytes through line-ending normalization or a copy fault.
A required V3 context could fail on the publication PR for a reason unrelated to its content (runner drift).
Until a V3 protection change (RD4), the published inputs on main are protected only by review and the pull-request-base rule of the workflow.
decisions: 1A, 2B and the I2-C admission decision apply unchanged.

RD1 (a) 2B set plus main README; RD2 (a) one PR; RD3 (a) TODO stays on the development branch; RD4 (a) protection deferred to a V3 trust change before I2-F; RD5 (a) bundle on the development branch first; RD6 merge commit.
